This forces one adjacent order divisible by p without narrowing the original type exponents.

The square quotient is identified as a presented group using the two computed commutator translations. Supported independent edge kernels give the lower bound, and two normal cyclic layers give the matching upper bound for every positive odd ell_1, ell_2 and d >= 1.

The marked square quotient and the two dihedral edge kernels satisfy the complete supported-kernel theorem included in this common paper; this proves every subset intersection and the exact adjacent orders.
The square quotient is abelian by dihedral; the two cyclic normal layers prove solvability without an unsupported restriction on the prime factors of ell_1 and ell_2.
Substitute ell_1 = p and ell_2 = 1 in the complete preceding presentation theorem; the full stated parameter range is retained.

The literal source word w has w^2 = 1 in the exact order-384 seed; killing a sends w to a reflection. The complete presentation extension therefore works for every s >= 2; three small executions are diagnostics for the uniform written argument.
